name: SSSI guidance collection
fact: Published 20 April 2026; collection groups current SSSI consent, assent, condition and designation guidance.
gate: Collection is procedural context, not a site-specific consent decision.

name: SSSI new sites and changes
fact: Updated 15 July 2026; Natural England may notify, vary or exceptionally de-notify SSSIs.
gate: Current designation state must be checked; historic designation alone may be insufficient.

name: SSSI condition assessments
fact: Published 20 April 2026; Natural England uses condition categories including favourable, recovering, declining, part destroyed and destroyed.
gate: Condition category is not a planning permission decision.

name: SSSI consent advice
fact: Published 20 April 2026; quick-check advice does not itself grant consent and statutory notice remains required.
gate: Advice service or quick check cannot be stored as consent.

name: SSSI assent advice
fact: Published 20 April 2026; public bodies must seek assent or advice where activities are likely to damage SSSI interest.
gate: Assent process is separate from general planning status.

name: SSSI public body responsibilities
fact: Updated 20 April 2026; public bodies must conserve and enhance SSSI features and request assent for damaging activities.
gate: Public-body duties do not imply a proposal-specific decision.

name: SSSI land management and consent
fact: Updated 20 April 2026; certain operations on SSSI land need Natural England consent and other permissions may still be required.
gate: Natural England consent does not replace planning or other legal permissions.

name: Scheduled monument consent service
fact: Works that damage, alter or add to a scheduled monument require scheduled monument consent in advance; in England Historic England handles applications on behalf of DCMS.
gate: Planning permission and scheduled monument consent are separate regimes.

name: Historic environment PPG
fact: Government PPG says World Heritage Sites and settings or buffer zones are protected through statutory designations and the planning system.
gate: Heritage status requires significance and setting assessment; designation alone does not settle a proposal.

name: TPO consideration screen
fact: Planning Data design research identifies TPO legislation and the order document as the legal protection mechanism.
gate: Design-stage material supports data modelling, not parcel legal conclusions.

name: Historic parks and gardens consideration
fact: Planning Data identifies registered parks and gardens as a heritage constraint and input to local plans.
gate: Design-stage consideration is not exact parcel policy evidence.

name: SAC planning consideration
fact: Planning Data classifies SACs as environmental constraints under the Habitats Regulations and an input to plan-making.
gate: Design-stage metadata does not replace current Natural England or HRA evidence.

name: SPA planning consideration
fact: Planning Data classifies SPAs as environmental constraints under the Habitats Regulations and an input to plan-making.
gate: Design metadata is not a project HRA or consent decision.

name: National nature reserves consideration
fact: Planning Data treats NNRs as environmental constraints and inputs to local-plan work.
gate: Design-stage metadata is not exact legal effect for a parcel.
